title: Check yourself: Choosing between similar features and combining them

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team must make sure that Claude never touches a file named `.env`. Which feature gives the guarantee?

options.text: A line in CLAUDE.md that forbids the edit
options.says: Ruled out because such an instruction "is a request, not a guarantee".

options.text: A hook on the `PreToolUse` event that rejects it
options.says: The page says "A `PreToolUse` hook that blocks the edit is enforcement."

options.text: A skill that explains why the file is private
options.says: Ruled out because with a skill, "Claude interprets the instructions; outcome can vary."

options.text: An output style that tells Claude to refuse
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude follows both as instructions, so neither is enforced."

questions.stem: A research task reads dozens of files and only the conclusions matter to the main conversation. Which feature fits?

options.text: A line in CLAUDE.md, which is loaded in full at the launch of each session
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "Put it in CLAUDE.md if Claude should always know it", and conclusions of one task are not such a rule.

options.text: A skill, which adds everything that it reads to the main window as well
options.says: Ruled out because a skill "adds to your main window".

options.text: A hook, which runs a script once per session when the work starts
options.says: Ruled out because a hook is for "when the action must happen the same way every time and doesn't need Claude to think".

options.text: A subagent, which works in its own window and hands back only a summary
options.says: The page says to use a subagent "when you need context isolation or when your context window is getting full".

questions.stem: A team connects Claude to its database and wants the model to use the tables and queries well. What does the page suggest?

options.text: Only an MCP server, since it provides everything that the work needs
options.says: Ruled out because MCP provides "Tools and data access", not knowledge of the schema and patterns.

options.text: MCP for access, and a skill for the schema and patterns
options.says: The page says "These solve different problems and work well together", with MCP for the connection and a skill that "can hold the team's database schema and query patterns".

options.text: Only a skill, since a skill can run the queries itself
options.says: Ruled out because a skill provides "Knowledge, workflows, reference material", and the connection to the external system comes from MCP.

options.text: A plugin, because plugins replace both of them
options.says: Ruled out because "Each extension solves a different problem", and a plugin only packages them.

concepts: Hook or skill, as the page teaches it
MCP or skill, as the page teaches it
Skill or subagent, as the page teaches it
